description: Open, machine-readable pricing data for LLM and AI APIs.

models.notes: Anthropic lists base input, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache hit, and output rates. cache_write stores the 5-minute write rate; cache_write_1h stores the 1-hour write rate. Batch input and output are 50% of Standard; prompt-cache multipliers stack with the Batch discount.

conditional_usage_allowances.note: Conditional short-term trial only: new AWS customers using the Paid plan can receive 1,000 Detect Document Text pages per month for three months. This is not an unconditional recurring free tier and is separate from general AWS promotional credits.

models.notes: Amazon Textract DetectDocumentText is the synchronous Basic OCR text-extraction API operation, not an LLM model. StartDocumentTextDetection is the asynchronous document-text operation and has matching regional Price List rates, but is not introduced as a separate identity in this DetectDocumentText-only onboarding. AWS counts PNG, TIFF, and JPEG images as one page and each PDF page as one processed page. Blank-page and failed-page billing edge semantics were not explicitly verified. AnalyzeDocument, Forms, Tables, Queries, Expense, Lending, Signatures, and Custom Adapters are excluded.

price_records.billing_note: Standard paid pricing is graduated monthly: USD 1.50 per 1,000 pages for the first 1,000,000 pages and USD 0.60 per 1,000 pages above 1,000,000 in most listed commercial regions. Region adjustments preserve the different US West (N. California) and GovCloud rates.
Standard paid graduated rate above 1,000,000 pages per month; regional multipliers preserve official region-specific SKU rates.

models.notes: Microsoft Azure Document Intelligence Read uses the exact GA model ID prebuilt-read with the 2024-11-30 API. This record admits only Standard S0 Basic OCR public retail pricing for 31 commercial ARM regions returned by the official Retail Prices API. F0, Batch Read, Government cloud, Layout, specialized prebuilt models, custom models, add-ons, Azure OpenAI, and Microsoft Copilot are not admitted. Current commercial rows have the same two rates but region-specific effectiveStartDate values from 2022-03-01 through 2025-02-01, so no single effective_from is asserted. PDF pages and TIFF images count as pages; each Excel worksheet and PowerPoint slide counts as one page; Word and HTML count in blocks of up to 3,000 characters. Blank-page, failed-request, partial-failure, and sub-1K rounding semantics remain unverified.

price_records.billing_note: Standard S0 Read public retail pricing is graduated monthly: USD 1.50 per 1,000 pages for the first 1,000,000 pages. calendar_month is the existing monthly cost-normalization contract and does not assert a universal Azure invoice-cycle start date.
Standard S0 Read graduated public retail rate above 1,000,000 pages per month: USD 0.60 per 1,000 pages across the admitted commercial regions.

models.notes: Cohere official pricing page states Aya Expanse 8B and 32B API pricing is $0.50/1M input and $1.50/1M output.

Cohere lists command-a-plus-05-2026 as Live and available through standard API endpoints, with no deprecation date. Its model page says both trial and production keys are free until rate limits are reached, while general pricing documentation says generative models including Command A+ are priced per token and the public pricing page says production keys are billed pay-as-you-go without publishing a Command A+ token rate. Standard Model Vault is a separate managed deployment option and lists Command A+ at $57.50 per XL instance-hour. V1 keeps Standard token, cached-input, and Batch prices null; null is not zero.
Cohere official pricing page lists Command R+ 08-2024 at $2.50/1M input tokens and $10.00/1M output tokens.

Cohere Parse v5 is generally available through the Cohere Parse API as parse-v5.0 at $1.50 per 1,000 pages. The public official sources do not publish a separate async or Batch API rate, page-count tier, or API free allowance. The free Cohere Space is a product demo, not a free API billing tier.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash was released on 2026-09-10. The official API model name is deepseek-flash and the pricing page identifies the served model version as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. V1 compatibility pricing uses the conservative Peak rate. Off-peak is 50% of Peak; Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday. The new rates took effect at 2026-09-10T04:00:00Z.

Native V4 Flash Peak and Off-peak rates took effect at 2026-08-16T16:00:00Z. DeepSeek retired V4 Flash on 2026-09-10; the legacy API name remains temporarily accepted, but current requests are served and billed as deepseek-flash. The canonical price fields retain the model's native historical schedule, while lifecycle redirect metadata identifies the current billing target.

DeepSeek retired V4 Flash Vision Exp on 2026-09-10. The legacy API name deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp remains temporarily accepted, but requests are served by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and billed at the Flash price. The projected Peak and Off-peak rates therefore come from the redirect billing target, not from an active experimental model.

DeepSeek's current Pricing page and 2026-09-10 Changelog state that V4 Pro will continue after 2026-09-14 with billing unchanged. The earlier news announcement describing a 2026-09-14 redirect to V4.1 Flash has therefore been superseded and is not represented as a scheduled transition. V1 compatibility pricing uses the conservative Peak rate; Off-peak is 50% of Peak.

Google Cloud Document AI Enterprise Document OCR uses the exact processor type OCR_PROCESSOR. This record covers Basic OCR only, excludes OCR add-ons and all specialized processors, and is separate from the Google Gemini model API. Pricing is graduated by pages processed in a monthly billing cycle; the official documentation does not identify the aggregation entity, so usage_scope is unknown.

price_records.billing_note: The first 1,000 pages in the monthly billing cycle are free. The official pages do not identify whether aggregation is by billing account, project, processor, or region, so usage_scope remains unknown.
Graduated monthly rate for cumulative pages above the first 1,000 through 5,000,000 pages: USD 1.50 per 1,000 pages.
Graduated monthly rate for cumulative pages above 5,000,000: USD 0.60 per 1,000 pages.

Declarative price_records preserve Standard, Batch, Flex, and Fast short/long pricing, the whole-request 272K input-token threshold, cache-write charges, regional data-residency uplift, and the Fast EU data-residency exclusion. models.notes: Available on the xAI API since 2026-08-12. V1 stores short-context pricing. Canonical Pricing V2 tiers model standard prompt tokens < 200K and long-context prompt tokens >= 200K. Total prompt tokens include cached and non-cached prompt tokens, and the selected tier applies to the whole request. The xAI model page marks Batch API as not supported, so Batch fields remain null.

Released on 2026-09-21 and available on the public xAI API. Supports text and image input with text output; reasoning efforts are low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. Global Standard rates use the short tier through 200,000 total prompt tokens and the long tier above 200,000; cached prompt tokens count toward the threshold and the selected tier prices the whole request. Grok 4.7 Fast is twice the Standard token rates but is available only in Cursor and Grok Build, not on the public xAI API, so it is excluded from public pricing rows. Batch API is not supported, no separate cache-write price is published, and the US regional endpoint applies a 1.10x premium to input, cached input, and output tokens, including long-context rates.
